attempts.narrative: The authored lesson landed on turn 1: Prankster Coaching went into Choice Scarf Sawk and the boosted Close Combat took Magearna from 80 to 16 in one hit. Nidoking was then one-shot by an Iron Fist Fire Punch the moment it switched in, Celebi died to a 4x U-turn plus Close Combat, and Whimsicott was removed by a 4x Poison Jab. Spiritomb carried the fight because Ghost is immune to every Fighting attack on the roster and to Throh's Body Slam - it finished at 40/68 having been hit only by Knock Off. Alakazam cleaned Machop and Throh. Three player faints against six.
attempts.note: Kept independent of the neighbouring Lilith battle, as the dossier requires. No merged twelve-member party.

strategy_checks.check: Prankster Riolu converts Coaching into an actual later physical attack, especially Scarf Mold Breaker Sawk
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1: Coaching targeted Sawk (+Attack, +Defense), and Sawk's Close Combat the same turn dealt 64 to an 80 HP Magearna. The recipient choice was correct - Sawk is the Scarf body that can use the boost immediately.

strategy_checks.check: Do not repeatedly coach an unavailable or protected attack
strategy_checks.evidence: Riolu was knocked out on turn 1 after a single Coaching, so no repeat occurred. It also did not waste the turn on Protect behind a Focus Sash.

strategy_checks.check: Native order, the Choice lock and survival determine the payoff
strategy_checks.evidence: Sawk stayed locked on Close Combat for three turns, including into a Spiritomb that is outright immune to it. Brenden then withdrew Sawk on turn 5 to clear the lock and brought it back with a fresh choice, which it used on a 4x Poison Jab into Whimsicott. That is correct Choice management by the trainer rather than a lock violation.

strategy_checks.check: No Guard Machop supplies an anti-evasion line
strategy_checks.result: PASS, though not via No Guard
strategy_checks.evidence: Machop never used Dynamic Punch - correctly, because its only available target was a Ghost that Fighting cannot touch. It used Knock Off twice instead and stripped Spiritomb's Leftovers. Choosing the one move that works against a Fighting-immune body is the right call; the No Guard accuracy branch simply had no board that needed it.

strategy_checks.check: Inner Focus Throh supplies an anti-flinch and critical-hit line; Bulk Up behind a real opportunity
strategy_checks.evidence: Throh entered on turn 8 opposite a +1 Spiritomb and a Life Orb Alakazam, used Protect once with real payoff, and died. It correctly declined Bulk Up with no safe turn. Inner Focus was never tested because I brought no flinch move.

strategy_checks.check: Stufful's Brick Break adds screen removal to the Fluffy/Bulk Up reserve
strategy_checks.evidence: Brick Break was used as damage on turn 6; I had no screens up, so the removal half was untestable. Bulk Up was correctly declined at 20/86 with lethal damage incoming.

strategy_checks.check: Monferno uses Iron Fist Fire Punch/Mach Punch, Close Combat and U-turn rather than duplicating Brick Break
strategy_checks.evidence: Fire Punch one-shot a switching-in Nidoking on turn 2, and on turn 3 Monferno U-turned out of an incoming Psychic for 4x damage on Celebi and a free pivot. Two different tools, both used well - the best sequencing on Brenden's side.

strategy_checks.check: Special damage bypasses Coaching's Defense gain (the authored crack)
strategy_checks.evidence: My entire party attacked specially. Coaching's Defense half never mattered; only its Attack half did, exactly as the crack predicts.

protect_ledger.payoff: real - blocked a Moonblast that was 2x and lethal at 20/86
real - blocked a 2x Psychic from a Life Orb Alakazam on the turn it entered

ai_observations: No defect. Three decisions were notably good: Machop declining its STAB Dynamic Punch for Knock Off against a Fighting-immune Ghost, Monferno U-turning out of an incoming super-effective Psychic, and Brenden withdrawing a burned Choice-locked Sawk to clear the lock and then re-deploying it onto a 4x Poison Jab target.
source_book_mismatch: Same pattern as E0035 Laura. The authored plan states 'Medium levels 22/25/23/25/25/24 at cap20', but the resolved Medium levels are 20/23/21/23/23/22 - exactly two lower across all six, because the offsets are 2/5/3/5/5/4 and Medium subtracts 2 from cap+offset. Two consecutive Dewford Gym rooms show the same two-level gap between the plan prose and the offsets, which suggests the prose for this whole room set was written against cap+offset without the Medium subtraction. This is a reconciliation item for the team owner; I did not resolve it, because raising six members by two is far beyond this pass's calibration mandate.
level_changes: none. Won on the first attempt but with three player faints out of six, which is the brief's 'won after a real fight' band and meets the AGENTS.md three-faint expectation. Every one of those faints came from a different opponent using a different tool - a Coached Close Combat, an Iron Fist Fire Punch on a switch-in, a 4x U-turn and a 4x Poison Jab. Keep the authored offsets (2/5/3/5/5/4), subject to the mismatch noted above.
cooler_note: A purposeful physical school is a legitimate room identity and this one is well executed - Coaching into a Choice Scarf body is a real doubles engine, and Monferno's pivoting gave the fight shape. Asking whether it could be cooler: the honest answer is that Brenden and Laura are two six-member all-Fighting rooms back to back, and I beat both with the same six Pokemon without changing a single slot. That is the design problem, and it is a room-set problem rather than a team problem. Within this team specifically, the one structural weakness is that a Ghost body turns off five of the six members' primary STAB at once; Stufful's Payback and Machop's Knock Off are the only Dark answers and both are weak. A concrete suggestion for a later pass (not applied here): give one member a genuine answer to a Ghost wall - Monferno already carries Fire Punch and is the natural home for a second non-Fighting attack - so that the obvious Ghost counterplay costs the player something instead of being free. Keep Riolu, the Coaching plan and the Choice Scarf Sawk; that trio is the most memorable thing in the room.
